summary: Russia is legally ambiguous and potentially restrictive for the roof rat, and importing one from abroad is currently effectively banned. The good news first: R. rattus is NOT on the federal list of animals prohibited from private keeping (Government Disposition No. 1163-r of 8 May 2025, in force 1 Sept 2025, which replaces Decree No. 795/2019, its only rodent entry is American porcupines, so the genus Rattus is absent). But absence from that ban does NOT make a roof rat a recognized 'domestic pet.' Unlike the ordinary fancy rat (R. norvegicus domestica), which is universally treated as an unregulated companion animal, R. rattus has no legally recognized domesticated status, so the Gemini DR reads it as defaulting to Federal Law No. 52-FZ 'On Wildlife.' Article 26 of that law lets you keep/breed 'objects of the animal world' in an 'artificially created habitat' (a cage counts) only with a permit from the regional Rosprirodnadzor, making private keeping a legal gray zone subject to regional-inspector discretion, with administrative fines (Art. 7.11 KoAP RF) and confiscation if challenged. Selling or giving any rodent additionally requires a Veterinary Accompanying Document (VSD) generated in the state FSIS 'Mercury' (Меркурий) traceability system run by Rosselkhoznadzor; hobbyists comply via a state vet clinic (SBBZh). Domestic transport needs the same VSD (Form 1 inter-regional, Form 4 local) and is otherwise lightly formalized (rodents may travel as baggage, ≤2 per ticket, carrier bears no liability). IMPORT is the hard wall: a Rosselkhoznadzor directive of 2 June 2022 (Mpox response) bans import of ALL rodents except for laboratories, zoos, circuses, and zooteaters, so private importation of a pet roof rat is currently prohibited. R. rattus is also on the SEVIN Top-100 invasive-species advisory list and is a state-mandated agricultural pest (deratization), which carries no keeping ban but reinforces the absolute rule: never release one.

keep.why: R. rattus is NOT on the federal prohibited-keeping list (Disposition 1163-r of 08.05.2025, in force 01.09.2025, replacing Decree 795/2019, the only Rodentia entry is American porcupines, so keeping is not federally banned outright). BUT absence from that list does not confer 'domestic pet' status. Because R. rattus has no recognized domesticated subspecies in Russian law (unlike R. norvegicus domestica, kept freely with no permit), the DR reads it as defaulting to an 'object of the animal world' under Federal Law No. 52-FZ 'On Wildlife.' Article 26 permits keeping/breeding wildlife in 'semi-free conditions and an artificially created habitat' (a residential cage qualifies) ONLY with a permit from the regional Rosprirodnadzor. Keeping without that permit is an administrative offense under Art. 7.11 KoAP RF (fines 500–1,000 RUB for citizens; 10,000–20,000 RUB for legal entities) and can trigger judicial confiscation. The SEVIN Top-100 invasive listing and the agricultural-pest (deratization) classification carry no keeping ban but underscore the absolute no-release rule. 'Unclear/low' because whether a regional Rosprirodnadzor inspector actually applies the Art. 26 wildlife-permit requirement to a captive-bred, multi-generation decorative roof rat, versus deferring it to unregulated companion-animal status like the fancy rat, is undefined in statute and turns on discretionary regional interpretation.
keep.governing_law: Federal Law No. 498-FZ 'On Responsible Treatment of Animals' Art. 10 + Disposition No. 1163-r (08.05.2025), Rattus NOT listed; Federal Law No. 52-FZ 'On Wildlife' (24.04.1995) Art. 26 (permit to keep wildlife in an artificial habitat); Art. 7.11 KoAP RF (penalties).

breed.why: Breeding follows keeping. If a regional Rosprirodnadzor classifies captive-bred R. rattus as an 'object of the animal world,' then breeding it in captivity strictly requires the Art. 26 permit of Federal Law No. 52-FZ (the same wildlife-in-an-artificial-habitat authorization as keeping), and the applicant must show enclosures secure enough to prevent escape into the ecosystem plus humane-husbandry compliance under 498-FZ. Commercial-scale breeding adds a second layer: sanitary-epidemiological compliance and routine veterinary inspection under the Law on Veterinary Medicine (No. 4979-1) and SanPiN rules (rodents are regulated as susceptible hosts for listeriosis/trichinellosis). There is no dedicated USDA-style 'pet-rodent breeder licence,' but a commercial breeder must maintain dual compliance (Rosprirodnadzor enclosure standards + Rosselkhoznadzor sanitary standards). Confidence medium because the underlying wildlife-classification question (which determines whether the Art. 26 permit applies at all) is itself unresolved.
breed.governing_law: Federal Law No. 52-FZ Art. 26 (captive-breeding permit if classed as wildlife); Federal Law No. 498-FZ (husbandry/welfare); Law on Veterinary Medicine No. 4979-1 (commercial sanitary/vet oversight).

sell_give.why: Any transfer of ownership of an animal, sale OR gift, requires a Veterinary Accompanying Document (VSD). Government Decree No. 2463 of 31.12.2020 (Retail Trade Rules, Section IX) mandates that the seller provide a veterinary certificate confirming the species' health and origin and that the species is not on the prohibited list. Critically, VSDs are electronic, generated and tracked in the Federal State Information System (FSIS) 'Mercury' (Меркурий), administered by Rosselkhoznadzor under the Law on Veterinary Medicine No. 4979-1; anyone selling a rodent must be registered in Mercury, and there is NO hobbyist/small-breeder exemption. In practice hobbyists comply by taking the animal to a state veterinary clinic (SBBZh), which examines it and issues the VSD for a nominal fee, transferring the animal from the seller's registered address to the buyer's. High confidence: veterinary traceability for rodents is strictly enforced regardless of domestic-vs-wild taxonomy. (Open practical question: how strictly regional vets enforce VSDs for non-commercial free gifting between private individuals in the same municipality.)
sell_give.governing_law: Government Decree No. 2463 (31.12.2020) Section IX (Retail Trade Rules, vet documents for animal sale); Law on Veterinary Medicine No. 4979-1 (VSD / FSIS Mercury); Federal Law No. 498-FZ Art. 10.

transport.why: Two very different pictures. DOMESTIC transit is restricted-but-formalized: it requires an electronic VSD (Form 1 for inter-regional movement, Form 4 for intra-regional) verifying health and origin from an epizootically safe area; rodents may otherwise be carried on long-distance trains (Russian Railways) as baggage, limited to 2 small animals per ticket, with the carrier legally absolved of all liability for the animal's injury, illness, loss, or death (Art. 8, Charter of Railway Transport). INTERNATIONAL import is the hard wall: a Rosselkhoznadzor directive of 2 June 2022 (issued in response to the global Mpox outbreak) bans the import of ALL rodents into Russia except specimens destined for laboratory research, zoos, zoological gardens, circuses, and zooteaters, which excludes private pet/personal/breeding imports entirely, with no recognized exception for 'tame' or captive-bred status. Even authorized institutional imports face multi-tiered quarantine (in the exporting country plus a second Rosselkhoznadzor-supervised domestic quarantine) with mandatory Mpox laboratory testing at the owner's expense. This emergency directive overrides the general EAEU customs allowances (the Form 41 zoo/exotic certificate and the CTS 317/2010 Ch. 15 simplified travellers' regime are rendered moot for private rodent import). Therefore private import of R. rattus is currently effectively PROHIBITED; domestic movement is restricted by the VSD requirement. Never release a nonnative.
transport.governing_law: Rosselkhoznadzor import-restriction directive (02.06.2022, rodents & primates, Mpox); Law on Veterinary Medicine No. 4979-1 + VSD Forms 1/4; Charter of Railway Transport Art. 8 (RZD baggage rules); EAEU CTS Decision 317/2010 (general regime, overridden for import).

restrictions.summary: If a regional Rosprirodnadzor treats captive-bred R. rattus as an 'object of the animal world' (the DR's reading, because it lacks recognized domestic status), then keeping or breeding it in a residential cage ('artificially created habitat') needs a Rosprirodnadzor permit under Art. 26 of Federal Law No. 52-FZ. To obtain it the applicant must document escape-proof enclosures and humane husbandry meeting zoological/sanitary standards. Keeping without the permit is an administrative offense under Art. 7.11 KoAP RF (fines 500–1,000 RUB for citizens; 10,000–20,000 RUB for legal entities) and can lead to judicial confiscation. Whether this permit is in fact demanded for a decorative captive-bred roof rat (vs. unregulated companion-animal treatment like the fancy rat) is the central open question.
steps: Determine with the regional Rosprirodnadzor whether captive-bred decorative R. rattus is treated as an 'object of the animal world' (wildlife) or deferred to companion-animal status like R. norvegicus
If treated as wildlife: apply to the regional Rosprirodnadzor for an Art. 26 permit to keep/breed wildlife in an artificially created habitat, documenting escape-proof enclosures and humane husbandry
Maintain secure, fail-safe containment (R. rattus is a state-recognized invasive pest, escape/release is multiply unlawful)

restrictions.summary: Any transfer of ownership (sale OR gift) and any movement of a rodent requires an electronic Veterinary Accompanying Document (VSD) generated in the FSIS 'Mercury' (Меркурий) system run by Rosselkhoznadzor, Form 1 for inter-regional movement, Form 4 for intra-regional. There is no hobbyist exemption; in practice a private keeper takes the animal to a state veterinary clinic (SBBZh), which examines it and issues the VSD for a nominal fee. Retail sale also falls under Decree 2463/2020 Section IX (vet certificate of health/origin + confirmation the species isn't prohibited).
steps: Register in (or have the issuing state vet act through) the FSIS Mercury system
Take the rat to a state veterinary clinic (SBBZh) for clinical examination
Obtain the electronic VSD (Form 1 inter-regional / Form 4 local) before sale, gift, or movement
For a retail sale, also provide the buyer the vet certificate and species/care information per Decree 2463/2020 §IX

restrictions.summary: IMPORT of any rodent into Russia by a private individual is currently effectively prohibited. A Rosselkhoznadzor directive of 2 June 2022 (Mpox response) restricts rodent import to specimens destined for laboratories, zoos, zoological gardens, circuses, and zooteaters only, no private pet/personal/breeding import, and no 'tame'/captive-bred exception. Authorized institutional imports require quarantine in the exporting country plus a second Rosselkhoznadzor-supervised domestic quarantine with Mpox laboratory testing at the owner's expense. This overrides the general EAEU customs/veterinary-certificate allowances.
steps: Do NOT attempt to import a pet roof rat into Russia, private rodent import is currently barred under the 2 June 2022 Rosselkhoznadzor directive (only lab/zoo/circus institutional imports are allowed, with quarantine + Mpox testing)
Confirm current status with Rosselkhoznadzor before any cross-border plan (the directive is an emergency measure and could be amended/repealed)
restrictions.where_to_file: Rosselkhoznadzor (Federal Service for Veterinary & Phytosanitary Surveillance), border veterinary control

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat. R. rattus is on the SEVIN 'Invasive Species of Russia Top-100' scientific advisory list and is a state-mandated agricultural pest subject to deratization. Releasing or abandoning a captive roof rat violates Federal Law 498-FZ (no abandonment), environmental-protection law (introducing a recognized invasive species), and sanitary-epidemiological rules, so enclosures must be exceptionally secure and escape-proof. The SEVIN listing/pest status carries no keeping ban itself.

inquiry_focus: (1) Rosprirodnadzor (the crux): does it classify captive-bred, multi-generation, decorative R. rattus (чёрная крыса) kept solely as an indoor pet as an 'object of the animal world' requiring an Art. 26 keeping/breeding permit under Federal Law 52-FZ, or is it administratively deferred to the unregulated companion-animal status of the fancy rat (R. norvegicus domestica)? (2) Rosselkhoznadzor: under the 2 June 2022 Mpox import directive, is there ANY waiver/quarantine pathway for a private citizen to import 1–3 captive-bred decorative R. rattus from a non-EAEU country as personal pets, or is all private (order Rodentia) import unconditionally suspended until the directive is repealed? (3) Rosselkhoznadzor (practice): to what extent do regional state vets (SBBZh) actually require an FSIS-Mercury VSD for non-commercial free gifting of a single offspring between private individuals within the same municipality, does the state differentiate commercial retail sale from private rehoming for epizootic tracking?
